lines.text: Evening. You'll be the one that got the pub, then. Mickey kept the mild on the left.
New face behind an old bar. That stool's got a bad leg, same as its owner.
You pulling pints now or just standing where Mickey stood? Either way, a bitter.
Shut the door, there's a gale off the harbour. So you're what the will dragged in.
We heard the nephew was coming. Nobody said he'd look so much like trouble's cousin.
A half of stout, when you find where he hid the glasses. Take your time, we all do.
Somebody had a busy night down Tannery Row, they're saying. Town this size, a name usually follows.
Word is the new fella at Mickey's keeps interesting hours. Wouldn't know him to look at, me.
June's girl saw a man in a runner's coat by the lockups past midnight. Could be anyone. Could be.
Police wagon went up Quay Street twice today. Twice is a pattern, once is a Tuesday.
They say whoever did the off-licence knew the tape gets changed Mondays. Local knowledge, that.
The Widow's lot were down the fish quay this morning, counting crates that weren't theirs.
Vane's solicitor bought the whole snug a round Thursday. Generosity like that has paperwork behind it.
Danny Ro's boys put a jukebox in the arcade. Plays one song. Loudly. All hours.
There's a copper asks questions in here Wednesdays. Drinks lime and soda. Tips like a magistrate.
Ferry ran late again. Harbour Board says weather. Harbour says the Board couldn't sail a bath.
The pirate station played requests till three. Half this town's courting on it and the other half's listening in.
Novak. Your usual stool's free, which is more than your uncle's debts are.
Here he is. Novak, the man himself. The pumps behaving for you tonight?
Evening, Novak. Rocco was in earlier, face like a wet fortnight. You'll know why, I expect.
Novak. Lena says you found the second ledger. She said it with her eyebrows, mind.
Ah, the landlord. Pour one for yourself, Novak, you look like the tide went out on you.
Heard your name twice today, Novak, and not in the parish notices either.
You want to walk softer, Novak. June was in the market and June has a voice on her.
Somebody matching your build was seen down Ironside. I said nothing. I'll want remembering for that.
The Widow asked after you by name, Novak. That's not a compliment in this town, that's a forecast.
Whatever went on at the lockups, Novak, the dogs knew you. Dogs talk, in their way.
Between us, Novak, the betting shop's paying out slow. Man came in white as a sheet Friday.
Your Rocco used to run with the dockside lot, Novak. Old news, but old news has long legs here.
They're saying Vane wants the Parade freehold. Lawyers first, then locksmiths, that's his order of service.
Novak, the camcorder fella from the wedding was filming gulls by the ferry. Caught more than gulls, I'd bet.
Father Emil knew your uncle better than the sermons let on. Ask him when the collection plate's empty.
Tom! Get in out of it. Kettle's mended, pumps aren't, story of the street.
There's Tom. Saved you the end seat. The dominoes want a fourth and your money's as good as anyone's.
Tom, son, you missed nothing. Match report: we lost, the pies fought back, the seagull won.
Evening, Tom. Ada was asking after you. Blushed like a postbox when I noticed, and so did she.
Tom. Your round, by my arithmetic. My arithmetic drinks bitter.
Tom, I'll say this once and to your face: whatever you're into, wash your hands before you pull my pint.
I told them my Tom wouldn't be mixed up in that. Then I remembered whose nephew you are.
You came in with the harbour on your boots again, Tom. I notice because I like you. Others notice for worse.
Tom, the detective was in asking after Thursday night. I remembered nothing so hard I sweated.
No names, Tom, but the man they're describing drinks in here and owes me a game of arrows.
Tom, keep it under your hat: the chippy's changing hands and the new lot count the peas.
The club's selling the town end, Tom. A fella from the Exchange was measuring it with his eyes.
Tom, June and the Widow were seen talking. Two minutes only. In this town that's a treaty.
The dog track's fixing the 8:15, Tom, regular as the tide. Third trap. You never heard it here.
Tom, the postcards in the kiosk have got saucier. Sold out by Friday, and the vicar bought the last one, for research.
New barmaid at the working men's club, Tom. Half the darts team's suddenly very committed to practice.
